evidence.note: 'Q3 on-time departures fell on the two routes diverted around the roadworks': thesis stated up front.
'On-time departures fell from 86% to 81% in Q3, and retiming the diverted routes is the Q4 test': quantifies the fall and states the recommendation.

'The council's 90% target counts on-time departures only, so lost mileage can rise unseen': a measurement caveat that does not follow from s-2 or lead into s-4; lost mileage never recurs in any later title.
'12 Cross-town and 14 Cross-town fell 14 and 11 points while the network fell 5': returns to on-time departures, re-stating figures already given in s-2's body and implied by s-1.
'Away from the roadworks the other six routes held between 85% and 90% on time': builds on s-4 (contrast group).
'Mill Street closed in three phases from 7 July, and routes 12 and 14 ran the diversion without retiming': cause, follows from s-5.
'Planning and the depot disagree on why 12 Cross-town fell a further 4 points in October': extends to October dispute, follows from s-6.
'Retiming 12 and 14 Cross-town for the diversion is the Q4 test, checked at the end of January': near-verbatim repeat of s-2's second clause.

rationale: Titles s-4 through s-7 build cleanly (drop, contrast, cause, open dispute) and the thesis appears at the start. But s-3's lost-mileage title does not connect to its neighbours and is never picked up again, breaking the argument between the summary and the results. And s-8 repeats s-2's recommendation almost word for word rather than advancing it.
